facts.fact: A KPI is defined by the vendor as a quantifiable measure of performance over a specific period of time and for a specific objective.
facts.quote: A KPI is a quantifiable measure of performance over a specific period of time, and for a specific objective.

facts.fact: The vendor states that the article covers 8 common KPIs for programmatic campaigns.
facts.quote: Here are 8 common KPIs for programmatic campaigns.

facts.fact: The vendor defines an impression as counted each time a creative is downloaded to the user's device and has started to load.
facts.quote: An impression is counted each time a creative is downloaded to the user’s device, and has started to load.

facts.fact: The vendor defines click-through rate (CTR) as the number of clicks an ad receives divided by the number of times the ad is shown, typically displayed as a percentage.
facts.quote: CTR is the number of clicks that an ad receives, divided by the number of times that the ad is shown.

facts.fact: The vendor states that click-through conversions usually record first-time clickers and are useful for tracking conversions that happen right away, without nurturing.
facts.quote: CTC usually records first-time clickers, and so it’s useful for tracking conversions that happen right away, without nurturing.

facts.fact: The vendor defines video completion rate (VCR) as measuring how many users watched a video ad from start to finish.
facts.quote: measures how many users watched a video ad from start to finish.

facts.fact: The vendor defines cost per completed view (CPCV) as an ad pricing model where marketers pay a publisher every time their video is watched from start to finish.
facts.quote: Cost per completed view (CPCV) is an ad pricing model where marketers pay a publisher every time their video is watched from start to finish.

facts.fact: The vendor states that CPCV is calculated by dividing the budget of an ad campaign by the total number of completed views.
facts.quote: CPCV is calculated by dividing the budget of an ad campaign by the total number of completed views.

facts.fact: The vendor states that cost per acquisition (CPA) is calculated by dividing the total campaign spend by the number of customers gained by that campaign.
facts.quote: CPA is calculated by dividing the total campaign spend by the number of customers that were gained by that campaign.

facts.fact: The vendor describes a brand lift study as measuring the impact of a campaign across all of a marketer's programmatic channels.
facts.quote: A brand lift study measures the impact of your campaigns across all your programmatic channels.

facts.fact: The vendor's article was published on 2023-07-11.
